lines.trans: Salma sent hot mint tea and warm almond biscuits for our composer!
Thank you both. Listen while I tap two rhythms on the table.
Does the ending go fast and bright, or gentle and slow?
Mazen's aunt wrote a light dancing beginning, like morning footsteps.
Then in the middle, the melody climbs up like afternoon conversation!
Exactly! So at six in the evening, how should a Friday waltz end?
Warm and unhurried—like friends lingering over their last cup of tea.
Yes! Repeat the opening four notes softly, one octave higher, and come home.
Just hearing you hum it in this glass room sounds wonderful, Suad!
Wait—right in bar twenty-eight, the melody lands squarely on middle D!
The exact silent key Tariq is repairing tomorrow morning!
No pressure for poor Tariq—the whole song rests on his tweezers!

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; the plural أغاني (aghaani) is the one you hear most.

examples.trans: This is an old song my grandmother loves.
We listen to songs in the car every morning.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Musical interval of eight scale steps.

examples.text: مدام سعاد عزفت نفس اللحن أوكتاف أعلى.
examples.trans: Madam Suad played the same melody one octave higher.

examples.text: الأوكتاف الوسطاني بالبيانو بده دوزان بسيط.
examples.trans: The middle octave on the piano needs a light tuning.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Warm spoken Levantine affirmation ('yes! / exactly!').

examples.text: أيوا، هاد هو اللحن اللي كنت أدور عليه!
examples.trans: Yes, that's the exact melody I was looking for!

examples.text: أيوا بالزبط، حط الكراسي جنب القوس.
examples.trans: Yes, right there—put the chairs beside the arch.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Musical rhythm or tempo pattern.

examples.text: إيقاع الفالس خفيف وبيرقص متل الموج.
examples.trans: A waltz rhythm is light and swaying like waves.

examples.text: دقت سعاد الإيقاع بأصابعها على طرف الطاولة.
examples.trans: Suad tapped the rhythm with her fingers on the edge of the table.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: The holy day in Islam and the weekend in Jordan.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Opening section of a song, book, or week.

examples.trans: The opening of the song is gentle and lifts the heart.

examples.text: من بداية الربيع، الساحة بتتعبى ورد.
examples.trans: From the start of spring, the courtyard fills with blossoms.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: General term for any kind of sweet, dry baked good like a cookie or biscuit.

examples.text: سلمى خبزت صينية بسكوت باللوز مع الشاي.
examples.trans: Salma baked a tray of almond biscuits to go with tea.

examples.text: حبة بسكوت دافية مع شاي بنعنع بتكفي.
examples.trans: One warm biscuit with mint tea hits the spot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بطيئة, plural: بطيئين).

examples.trans: Downtown traffic at noon is slow.
A slow step is better than rushing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببعت, بيبعت).

examples.trans: Last week I sent him a postcard.
She sent a kind thank-you note.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine preposition meaning 'without' or 'let's skip / no…' (قهوة بلا سكر 'coffee without sugar').

examples.text: بشرب الشاي بنعنع وبلا سكر لو سمحت.
examples.trans: I drink mint tea without sugar, please.

examples.text: بلا عجلة، قدامنا تلات أيام كاملة.
examples.trans: No rush—we have three full days ahead of us.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: A literal physical step or a metaphorical step in a process.

examples.trans: I heard footsteps on the wooden stairs.
We walked step by step in the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

خِلِص.gloss: to run out; be finished; end

meanings.en: to run out; be finished; end
meanings.note: Form I intransitive counterpart of transitive خلّص ('to finish something'): خلص الخبز means 'the bread has run out'.

examples.text: يلا نمشي قبل ما يخلص الخبز السخن.
examples.trans: Let's walk over before the hot bread sells out.

examples.text: خلصت القهوة، رح أعمل إبريق جديد.
examples.trans: The coffee ran out; I will make a fresh pot.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Essential Jordanian word used for giving directions ('go straight') or to mean doing something immediately.

examples.trans: Turn left and walk straight to the bridge.
Walk straight to the end of the street.

meanings.note: Past tense verb for knocking on a door, hammering a nail, or sometimes calling someone on the phone ('daqq 'ala').

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast!
The clock tower started chiming twelve.

meanings.note: Softly humming a melody without words.

examples.text: سمعنا دندنة هادية طالعة من غرفة البيانو.
examples.trans: We heard gentle humming coming from the piano room.

examples.text: دندنتها للحن خلت الغرفة كلها تبتسم.
examples.trans: Her humming of the melody made the whole room smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رائعة, plural: رائعين).

examples.trans: A wonderful choice with morning tea!
The weather in the courtyard today is splendid.

meanings.note: Describes a light, buoyant waltz melody.

examples.text: أول اللحن فيه نغمة خفيفة وراقصة.
examples.trans: The opening of the melody has a light, dancing lilt.

examples.text: الضو كان يرمي ظلال راقصة على حيط الحجر.
examples.trans: The lantern cast dancing shadows across the stone wall.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Solfege name standard in Arabic music education for the note D (ري الوسطى 'middle D').

examples.text: نغمة ري الوسطى هي المفتاح اللي كان ساكت.
examples.trans: Middle D is the exact key that was silent.

examples.text: الأغنية بتنزل بهدوء على نغمة ري بالأخير.
examples.trans: The song settles gently onto D near the end.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: From سكت, to fall silent: a person who says nothing, or a thing that makes no sound.

examples.trans: Why are you so quiet today? Is something wrong?
The phone has been silent since the morning.

meanings.note: Warm Jordanian word; plural سواليف (sawaaliif) means relaxed afternoon chats and stories.

examples.text: سواليف العصر مع كاسة شاي ما بتمل منها.
examples.trans: You never tire of afternoon conversation over a glass of tea.
We sat in the courtyard and the warm stories began.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سريعة, plural: سريعين).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
Quick service and a kind smile.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) of سمع ('hear/listen').

examples.text: سماع الموسيقى بهالغرفة الهادية بيرح البال.
examples.trans: Listening to music in this quiet room puts the mind at ease.
We were delighted to hear the good news.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صحاب.

examples.trans: Who is the owner of the blue suitcase?
We became friends from the first day.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصلح, بيصلح).

examples.trans: I fix pipes and chairs.
Yesterday you fixed the old heater.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضغوط.

examples.trans: The pressure valve on the boiler works.
Calm tea eases blood pressure.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعيد, بيعيد).

examples.trans: I will repeat the words the whole way!
Could you repeat the number, please?

meanings.note: Can mean physically high or loud (for a voice or sound).

examples.trans: What is that loud sound upstairs?
The wooden ceiling is high and sunny.

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصور.

examples.trans: We arrived at the guesthouse Monday afternoon.
Late-afternoon tea in the courtyard is a daily ritual.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Intransitive verb ('ili / byi'la) describing a melody, voice, or price rising.

examples.text: بنص الأغنية، اللحن بيعلى شوي شوي.
examples.trans: In the middle of the song, the melody climbs bit by bit.
The sound of rain on the window grew louder at night.

meanings.note: Arabic distinguishes father's sister (عمة, feminine of عمّ) from mother's sister (خالة).

examples.text: عمتي كانت تعزف عالبيانو كل يوم جمعة.
examples.trans: My paternal aunt used to play the piano every Friday.

examples.text: هاد الدفتر الأخضر هدية من عمتي.
examples.trans: This green notebook is a gift from my aunt.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Musical loanword (from French valse) for a triple-time piano or orchestral waltz.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد فالس هادي بغرفة القزاز.
examples.trans: Suad played a gentle waltz in the sunroom.

examples.text: عنوان الورقة القديمة هو فالس الساحة.
examples.trans: The title on the old sheet is Courtyard Waltz.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Literally 'sitting', but widely used as an auxiliary participle to denote continuous present action (like English '-ing').

examples.trans: Who is sitting in our courtyard under the tree?
We are sitting having tea.

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كاسات.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
He poured half a glass of orange juice.

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: The main interrogative word for asking about manner or state.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألحان.

examples.trans: She played old melodies on the piano.
This gentle tune is familiar to me.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.text: ريحة اللوز المحمص طالعة من فرن سلمى.
examples.trans: The aroma of toasted almonds is drifting out of Salma's oven.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز بتعطي تارت الليمون قرمشة طيبة.
examples.trans: An almond crust gives the lemon tart a delicious crunch.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic conservatory/musicians' term (from Italian misura) for one bar of music.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد أول أربع مازورات من الفالس.
examples.trans: Suad played the first four bars of the waltz.

examples.text: اللحن بيوقف بنص المازورة الرابعة والعشرين.
examples.trans: The melody stops in the middle of the twenty-fourth bar.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مسكينة, plural: مساكين).

examples.trans: The poor gentleman was worried about the guesthouse.
He arrived in the rain, poor thing, and cold.

meanings.note: Describes bright morning light or an upbeat musical ending.

examples.text: النهاية السريعة بتعطي الأغنية طابع مشرق.
examples.trans: A fast ending gives the song a bright feel.

examples.text: صباح الأحد كان مشرق ودافي بالساحة.
examples.trans: Sunday morning was bright and warm in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Musical composer; feminine ملحنة (mulahhine).

examples.text: مدام سعاد صارت ملحنتنا الرسمية لليلة الافتتاح!
examples.trans: Madam Suad has become our official composer for opening night!

examples.text: الملحن كتب أول أربعة وعشرين مازورة بالحبر الأسود.
examples.trans: The composer wrote the first twenty-four bars in black ink.

meanings.note: Fine tweezers for delicate repair work, or small kitchen tongs.

examples.text: طارق طلب ملقط رفيع عشان يمسك الدبوس النحاس.
examples.trans: Tariq asked for thin tweezers to hold the tiny brass pin.

examples.text: البرغي الصغير ما بينمسك إلا بملقط.
examples.trans: That tiny screw can only be picked up with tweezers.

meanings.note: Lives in the chunk على مهل (or على مهلك), 'slowly, take your time'.

examples.trans: Walk slowly, the stairs are slippery.
Drive slowly, it is raining.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: A very common herb used in Levantine tea and cuisine.

examples.trans: Tea with fresh mint warms the heart.
We planted mint in the courtyard beside the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نغمات.

examples.text: سمع كل نغمة من البيانو بهدوء.
examples.trans: He listened quietly to every note of the piano.
The chime of the bell is gentle, not harsh.

meanings.note: Often used to mean 'the same' when followed by a noun, or as a reflexive.

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun; نهاية الأسبوع means 'weekend'. Plural: نهايات.

examples.trans: There is a new booking for the weekend.

examples.text: بالنهاية كل شي انحل على خير.
examples.trans: In the end everything worked out well.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: The guests will come down at half past seven.
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Masculine هادي ('quiet') is homographic with the feminine demonstrative هادي ('this'); context and agreement distinguish them cleanly.

examples.trans: The spot above the tree is very quiet.
We prepared the quiet attic room for you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The morning quiet of the courtyard is very peaceful.
We talked the matter through calmly and patiently.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian adjective from وسط ('middle'); pairs naturally with المفتاح الوسطاني and ري الوسطى.

examples.text: المفتاح الوسطاني بالبيانو كان عالق من الرطوبة.
examples.trans: The middle key on the piano was stuck from dampness.

examples.text: الطاولة الوسطانية بالساحة بتاخد أحلى شمس.
examples.trans: The middle table in the courtyard catches the nicest sunshine.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Warm Jordanian/Levantine thank-you when someone hands you food, tea, or help (short for يسلموا إيديك 'may your hands be blessed').

examples.trans: Thank you, Salma, for the hot tea!
Thank you, it smells wonderful!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
